title: Aragoz hand-puppet booth
summary: A squeaky-voiced glove puppet in a red cap pops up over a little booth and jokes with the crowd about daily life. Street performers in Egypt have played Aragoz for centuries, using a small reed in the mouth for his voice.
howToPlay: Read the scene and choose what Aragoz and his friends do.
Wit solves the puzzle; goodwill wins the crowd.
Answer the puzzle with a clear head and keep the crowd on your side.
Reach the last scene to see your stars.
rules: Hiding something never works for long.
Some endings are sweeter than others.
Both wit and goodwill are needed for three stars.
heritageNote: Aragoz is the glove puppet of Egypt: a wooden head, a red cap and a cloth cloak over the performer's hand, played from a small cloth booth with a high voice made by a small reed held in the mouth. It has been a street and fair entertainment for centuries, full of jokes about officials, neighbours and money, and it is recognised internationally as living heritage.
